Apomorphine is known to bind to Drd3, a subunit of the dopamine receptor, and this interaction is coupled via the Gi/go signaling pathway. The observed pathway indicates that Drd3, which is involved in dopamine receptor activity, is also participated by Drd4, suggesting a possible functional overlap or co-expression in the cellular context. This implies that Apomorphine may modulate Drd4 activity through the same signaling cascade, potentially influencing dopamine receptor function. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between Apomorphine and Drd4, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated. The presence of a binding interaction between Apomorphine and Drd3, along with the involvement of Drd4 in the same signaling pathway, provides a plausible basis for the proposed relationship.
